# Prefer undo over confirmation

Make reversible actions immediate with undo; ask for confirmation only when an action is irreversible or costly, and then name the consequence on the buttons.

## Why

External standard, not learned from the user's feedback. Routine confirmations train users to click through, so they stop protecting anything; undo recovers the mistakes confirmations miss.

## Prefer

- Run reversible actions immediately and offer undo in place.
- Reserve confirmation for irreversible or costly actions, such as destroying work or spending money.
- Label confirmation buttons with what will happen, such as Delete file and Keep file.

## Avoid

- Confirmation dialogs for routine, reversible actions.
- Yes, No, OK, or Confirm as confirmation choices.

## Use when

- An action deletes, overwrites, sends, or spends something.

## Do not use when

- Regulation or policy requires an explicit confirmation step.

## Sources

- NN/g: Confirmation Dialogs Can Prevent User Errors (If Not Overused) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/confirmation-dialog/

## Check

- Is the action reversible, and if so is undo offered instead of a confirmation?
- Is every remaining confirmation for an irreversible or costly action?
- Do confirmation buttons name their consequence?
